knowledge_point.title: Integrating an Algebraic Function With Positive Integer Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3x-1.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 48(3x-1)^{7}\,\text{d}x & =\int 48{u}^{7}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =48\cdot \frac{1}{3}\int {u}^{7}\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\cdot \frac{{u}^{8}}{8}+C \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{8}+C \\  & =2(3x-1)^{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-1)^{8}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-1)^{8}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =16(3x-1)^{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-1)+0 \\  & =16(3x-1)^{7}\cdot 3 \\  & =48(3x-1)^{7}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: All real x; C an arbitrary integration constant.
generation.sampling_policy: Vary positive constant magnitude b in 1..80. Keep source slope, exponent, outer coefficient, complete bank and ordered solution fixed. Hard is explicitly authored same-method calibration.

knowledge_point.title: Integrating an Algebraic Function With Positive Integer Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3x-44.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 48(3x-44)^{7}\,\text{d}x & =\int 48{u}^{7}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =48\cdot \frac{1}{3}\int {u}^{7}\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\cdot \frac{{u}^{8}}{8}+C \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{8}+C \\  & =2(3x-44)^{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-44)^{8}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-44)^{8}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =16(3x-44)^{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-44)+0 \\  & =16(3x-44)^{7}\cdot 3 \\  & =48(3x-44)^{7}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: All real x; C an arbitrary integration constant.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=56-2x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 16(56-2x)^{7}\,\text{d}x & =\int 16{u}^{7}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\int {u}^{7}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\int {u}^{7}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-8\cdot \frac{{u}^{8}}{8}+C \\  & =-{u}^{8}+C \\  & =-(56-2x)^{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-(56-2x)^{8}+C] & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(56-2x)^{8}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-8(56-2x)^{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(56-2x)+0 \\  & =-8(56-2x)^{7}\cdot (-2) \\  & =16(56-2x)^{7}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 48(3x-1)^{7}\,\text{d}x & =\int 48{u}^{7}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =48\cdot \frac{1}{3}\int {u}^{7}\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\cdot \frac{{u}^{8}}{8}+C \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{8}+C \\  & =2(3x-1)^{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-1)^{8}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-1)^{8}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =16(3x-1)^{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-1)+0 \\  & =16(3x-1)^{7}\cdot 3 \\  & =48(3x-1)^{7}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
